files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: P. Guerrero. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, propose one correcting journal entry.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 and paying in July. If one exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities; note that in some months every payroll run pays in-month.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, supporting contracts, and the GL. If it is absent, book ONE combined journal entry—do not duplicate an entry already posted. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month each prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after confirming the GL does not already contain the entry.
5. Inspect June vendor-bill documents against the GL coding. Verify each bill is charged to the correct expense account and reclass anything miscoded.
6. Prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis, only after items 1-5 have been booked.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Cirrus Metrics Inc. began in 2019 after its founders spent too many Monday mornings stitching together exports from billing, product, and customer-support systems. They believed operating teams needed a shared view of the business without maintaining a maze of spreadsheets, so they built a lightweight cloud application around that idea.

Today, Cirrus Metrics Inc. sells software that connects common business tools, standardizes recurring operating measures, and presents them through configurable dashboards and scheduled reports. Customers use the platform to monitor customer activity, service performance, and internal workflows. The product is designed for teams that want dependable answers but do not have a large data-engineering function.

The company remains small and practical by choice. Engineers sit close to implementation and support, while the commercial team mixes customer education with a consultative sales style. Product discussions are direct, documentation is taken seriously, and unusual customer requests tend to become lively cross-functional conversations. The team favors incremental releases over splashy launches.

The current focus is steady execution: improving integrations, refining onboarding, and making reports easier for nontechnical users to manage. Leadership is also tightening routine operating processes as the customer base grows. The business is an ordinary going concern, balancing product development, customer service, marketing, and the administrative work expected of a maturing SaaS company.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## What we are trying to do

Make Cirrus Metrics Inc. easier to recognize, easier to understand, and easier for operating teams to evaluate. The message should stay practical: connected metrics, less spreadsheet work, and reporting people can actually use.

## Priorities

- Refresh the brand system and core website language without turning the project into a wholesale repositioning.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, built around common reporting problems rather than product demos alone.
- Pilot partner co-marketing with a small group of implementation consultants and adjacent software providers.
- Develop customer stories that show the before-and-after workflow in plain language.
- Give sales a tighter set of one-page explainers for integrations, onboarding, and reporting use cases.

## Channel approach

Use email and LinkedIn to distribute practical guides, webinar clips, and customer examples. Keep search content focused on high-intent operational reporting topics. Test partner newsletters and joint events before committing to a broader program.

## Measures of progress

Track qualified conversations, webinar attendance and follow-up, partner-sourced interest, content engagement, and movement from initial evaluation into product review. Report results by quarter and include qualitative feedback from sales and customer success.

## Open items

Final sequencing depends on Q2 learnings, design capacity, and partner readiness. Owners and launch checkpoints still need confirmation.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your predecessor

P. Guerrero — a few things that will save you some hunting:

- The bank tends to place its own fees and charges near the end of the statement. We book those during close, not as they appear during the month, so do not overlook the last section.
- June got busy and some vendor-bill expense coding may be wrong. Use the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative, compare them with the ledger, and reclass where needed.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. The one-off items that arrived in June were never included, and they are the reason several variances look unusually large.
- Payroll is not on the usual in-month pattern this time: the second June run pays in early July. Check the payroll register before booking the accrual.
